key_insight: X-MuTeST combines LLM-provided high-level semantic explanations with attention-enhancing training to improve both performance and interpretability of hate speech detection across English, Hindi, and Telugu. The framework produces human-aligned explanations while boosting detection robustness for underexplored Indic languages.
problem_solved: Lack of accurate and explainable hate speech detection methods and benchmarks for underrepresented Indic languages (Hindi, Telugu) limits trustworthy moderation and cross-lingual evaluation.
method: Explainability-guided training: incorporate explanation signals during model training to align predictions with human-understandable rationales.
LLM-consulted explanations: use large language models to generate high-level semantic reasoning that informs or regularizes the classifier.
Attention-enhancing techniques + multilingual benchmark: combine attention methods with the new X-MuTeST dataset covering English, Hindi, and Telugu for evaluation.
impact: Enables practitioners to build more trustworthy, interpretable hate detection systems for multilingual contexts, especially for low-resource Indic languages, and provides a benchmark to compare explainability-aware models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: show LLM explanation generation feeding into explainability-guided training and attention module for the classifier.
Language map: icons/flags for English, Hindi, Telugu with dataset sizes and annotation quality badges.
Metric comparison bar chart: model accuracy vs. explainability alignment (e.g., faithfulness or human agreement) across baselines and X-MuTeST.
Example explanation card: original post, model label, attention heatmap, and LLM-generated rationale side-by-side.
paper_title: X-MuTeST: A Multilingual Benchmark for Explainable Hate Speech Detection and A Novel LLM-consulted Explanation Framework
paper_authors: Mohammad Zia Ur Rehman, Sai Kartheek Reddy Kasu, Shashivardhan Reddy Koppula, Sai Rithwik Reddy Chirra, Shwetank Shekhar Singh
